```mermaid
        C1["Your Bash shell is ONE persistent session for the whole task — a cd in one command carries over to every later command, including Write/Edit"]
        C2["cd dependencies/<repo> to explore a dependency's source? You are now inside it for every subsequent command until you cd out"]
        C3["Forgetting to cd back before writing outputs/* silently writes to dependencies/<repo>/outputs/* instead of the job's own outputs/ — the write itself succeeds, so nothing looks wrong, but the file is lost"]
        C4["Before ANY Write/Edit to outputs/ (response.md, pr_review.json, pr_review_comments/*.md, etc.): run pwd first and confirm you are at the job root, not inside dependencies/"]
        C5["If unsure or already deep in a dependency checkout: cd to the ABSOLUTE job root path shown in the very first tool result of this session before writing outputs/*"]

        C8["Git global flags like --no-pager go BEFORE the subcommand: git --no-pager diff ... is correct, git diff ... --no-pager errors out (git treats the trailing flag as a positional argument)"]
```

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory/
# teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file carries
# only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository event
# triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]  # dev leg; review/rework ride labels too
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  dedupe:
    # First-wins: the `issues` trigger fires on assigned AND labeled, so one
    # manual launch can dispatch two dev legs minutes apart (live gh-305 twin,
    # 2026-09-30: 36767724353 in_progress + 36767943650 pending behind the
    # concurrency group, both event=issues). The concurrency group only
    # SERIALIZES twins — this gate makes the younger run self-cancel when an
    # older live run of this workflow already anchors the same issue/pr.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status in_progress --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status queued    --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status pending   --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  factory:
    needs: dedupe
    if: needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true'
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA the `agents` submodule pins — a branch
    # ref executes the branch head at run start, and the head has since
    # renamed the reusable workflows away from factory/<name>.yml. This
    # commit has the called paths and the self-pin that checks out
    # factory-agents/ at the same SHA. Flip in lockstep with the
    # submodule when dmtools-agents#424 merges (bump the submodule,
    # then repoint this ref at the new SHA).
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@0176b270314aba9dcbd70732db558a156b03df04
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 0176b270314aba9dcbd70732db558a156b03df04
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
# DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY (pack registry base) is read by the factory from
# this repo's VARIABLE of the same name — see dmtools-agents#574.

Now let me analyze this change carefully. The PR adds a `dedupe` job to the `ai-teammate.yml` workflow. Let me look at the details:

```yaml
jobs:
  dedupe:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list ... --status in_progress ...
                    gh run list ... --status queued ...
                    gh run list ... --status pending ...
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

Issues to consider:

1. **Self-cancel race / fallthrough behavior**: When a duplicate is detected, the step sets `duplicate=true`, then calls `gh run cancel` on itself, then `exit 0`. The job continues (exits 0 → success). The `factory` job is skipped due to the `if`. But the run shows as "success" while also being cancelled — the `gh run cancel` is async; the run gets status cancelled eventually. This is a bit odd but works. Actually wait — there's a subtlety: `gh run cancel` cancels the entire run, which would cancel this very `dedupe` job mid-flight. But before that, the step writes `duplicate=true` and exits 0. When the run is cancelled, the `factory` job... hmm, the factory job's `if: needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true'` would prevent it from running anyway. Actually when a run is cancelled, GitHub cancels all pending jobs. So factory would be cancelled anyway. The `duplicate` output is belt-and-suspenders.

   Wait, actually there's a real concern: `gh run cancel` on the current run from within itself — does it work? Yes, it's a known pattern; the API accepts it and the run gets cancelled. Though there can be a race where the cancel API returns success but the run completes before cancellation takes effect. The `exit 0` ensures the job doesn't fail. But the run's conclusion would be "cancelled" — fine.

   Actually a subtle bug: if `gh run cancel` fails (e.g., permissions), the run continues as successful and factory is skipped via the output. OK, that's handled.

2. **ANCHOR mismatch between run-name token and displayTitle matching**: The dedupe matches the anchor token in `displayTitle`. The run-name is:
   ```
   ▶ {leg} (SM) · pr-{pr} or gh-{issue} · {title}
   ```
   or for issues events:
   ```
   '⚒️ dev' · gh-{issue.number}{: title}
   ```
   
   Wait — for `issues` events, the run name is `'⚒️ dev · gh-305: <issue title>'`. The displayTitle for a workflow run is the run name. So matching `test("(^|[^0-9])gh-305([^0-9]|$)")` — the title could contain "gh-305" elsewhere. The regex `(^|[^0-9])gh-305([^0-9]|$)` requires the token be delimited by non-digits. Reasonable.

   BUT: an important issue — the token `gh-<issue>` may legitimately appear in the issue TITLE itself! E.g., issue title "Fix gh-305 regression" — wait, but that would only match if the title contains the exact same anchor token as the current run's anchor. If issue #305's title mentions "gh-305"... unlikely coincidence but possible. More importantly: an issue whose title references the same issue number (e.g. rework labels re-fire with run name "🔧 rework · gh-305: Fix bug in gh-305"). Hmm, edge case. Not blocking.

3. **Match ignores the LEG dimension**: Two runs on the same issue with different legs (dev vs review) — e.g., dispatch dev leg for gh-305 while a review leg for gh-305 is in progress. Both have tokens `gh-305`. The dedupe would self-cancel the second leg even though it's a DIFFERENT leg (review vs dev). Is that a problem? The concurrency group already serializes them (cancel-in-progress: false), so they queue. With this gate, the second one (different leg!) self-cancels entirely rather than queueing. Hmm — is that intended? The PR title says "identical live leg self-cancels". But the gate doesn't compare legs — it only compares the anchor. # Control the concurrency of workflows and jobs

Manage which workflows and jobs can run simultaneously.

Copy markdown

## In this article

## Using concurrency in different scenarios

You can use `jobs.<job_id>.concurrency` to ensure that only a single job or workflow using the same concurrency group will run at a time. A concurrency group can be any string or expression. Allowed expression contexts: [`github`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#github-context), [`inputs`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#inputs-context), [`vars`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#vars-context), [`needs`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#needs-context), [`strategy`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#strategy-context), and [`matrix`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#matrix-context). For more information about expressions, see [Evaluate expressions in workflows and actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions).

You can also specify `concurrency` at the workflow level. For more information, see [`concurrency`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#concurrency).

This means that there can be at most one running job or workflow in a concurrency group at any time. When a concurrent job or workflow is queued, if another job or workflow using the same concurrency group in the repository is in progress, the queued job or workflow will be `pending`. By default, any existing `pending` job or workflow in the same concurrency group will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place.

To also cancel any currently running job or workflow in the same concurrency group, specify `cancel-in-progress: true`. - The concurrency group name is case insensitive. For example, `prod` and `Prod` will be treated as the same concurrency group.

The default behavior of GitHub Actions is to allow multiple jobs or workflow runs to run concurrently. The `concurrency` keyword allows you to control the concurrency of workflow runs.

```yaml
on:

    branches:

concurrency:

```


The `concurrency` key is used to group workflows or jobs together into a concurrency group. With `queue: max`, up to 100 jobs or workflow runs can wait in the concurrency group; once the queue is full, any additional runs are canceled.

To use concurrency to cancel any in-progress job or run in GitHub Actions, you can use the `concurrency` key with the `cancel-in-progress` option set to `true`:

🚨 **BLOCKING: The live-run check cannot see the twins it targets — group-serialized duplicates still run a second leg**

The gate lists only `in_progress`/`queued`/`pending` runs, but a same-anchor twin **cannot be live when this job evaluates**: per [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/using-concurrency), a run queued behind a `cancel-in-progress: false` group stays `pending` until the in-progress run **completes**, and only then do its jobs start. So the younger twin's `dedupe` job always executes *after* the older run finished — `LIVE` is 0 — and the duplicate leg runs anyway.

The cited incident proves the shape: twin `36767943650` was created +113s after holder `36767724353`, sat `pending` for 23 minutes, and never dequeued before being cancelled at 20:09:44 (holder completed 20:15:37). With this gate, its dedupe would have run at ~20:16, found the holder `completed` (not listed), and dispatched a second full dev leg. The gate's effective window is only the first ~minute of the older run's life (while its own `dedupe` step runs); a twin arriving later — the "minutes apart" case in the PR description — is invisible to it.

**Suggested fix (the two halves pair; neither alone suffices):**
1. Also match **recently completed** runs, so the dequed twin sees the just-finished holder: list `--status completed --created=>$(date -u -d '10 min ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)` and self-cancel on a match. This catches the serialized twin with true first-wins (the holder already ran).
2. See the comment on `select(.databaseId != $self)` — without the `<` fix there, the older run self-cancels on sight of a pending younger twin.

Alternative structural fix: dedupe at the event level — one manual launch fires both `assigned` and `labeled`, so gate one of them at trigger/`jobs.<job>.if` level (e.g. only `agent:review`/`agent:rework` labels launch legs) instead of trying to detect twins at run time, where the group guarantees they can't be seen live.

Secondary note: the match is leg-blind (anchor only) — with the completed-window fix, a legitimate review/rework leg dequeued just after a dev leg on the same issue would self-cancel too. If per-leg semantics are wanted, include the run-name leg marker (`⚒️`/`🔍`/`🔧`/`▶ <leg> (SM)`) in the token.

# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory/
# teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file carries
# only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository event
# triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]  # dev leg; review/rework ride labels too
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  dedupe:
    # First-wins: the `issues` trigger fires on assigned AND labeled, so one
    # manual launch can dispatch two dev legs minutes apart (live gh-305 twin,
    # 2026-09-30: 36767724353 in_progress + 36767943650 pending behind the
    # concurrency group, both event=issues). The concurrency group only
    # SERIALIZES twins — this gate makes the younger run self-cancel when an
    # older live run of this workflow already anchors the same issue/pr.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status in_progress --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status queued    --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status pending   --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  factory:
    needs: dedupe
    if: needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true'
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA the `agents` submodule pins — a branch
    # ref executes the branch head at run start, and the head has since
    # renamed the reusable workflows away from factory/<name>.yml. This
    # commit has the called paths and the self-pin that checks out
    # factory-agents/ at the same SHA. Flip in lockstep with the
    # submodule when dmtools-agents#424 merges (bump the submodule,
    # then repoint this ref at the new SHA).
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@0176b270314aba9dcbd70732db558a156b03df04
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 0176b270314aba9dcbd70732db558a156b03df04
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
# DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY (pack registry base) is read by the factory from
# this repo's VARIABLE of the same name — see dmtools-agents#574.

Now let me analyze this change carefully. The PR adds a `dedupe` job to the `ai-teammate.yml` workflow. Let me look at the details:

```yaml
jobs:
  dedupe:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list ... --status in_progress ...
                    gh run list ... --status queued ...
                    gh run list ... --status pending ...
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

Issues to consider:

1. **Self-cancel race / fallthrough behavior**: When a duplicate is detected, the step sets `duplicate=true`, then calls `gh run cancel` on itself, then `exit 0`. The job continues (exits 0 → success). The `factory` job is skipped due to the `if`. But the run shows as "success" while also being cancelled — the `gh run cancel` is async; the run gets status cancelled eventually. This is a bit odd but works. Actually wait — there's a subtlety: `gh run cancel` cancels the entire run, which would cancel this very `dedupe` job mid-flight. But before that, the step writes `duplicate=true` and exits 0. When the run is cancelled, the `factory` job... hmm, the factory job's `if: needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true'` would prevent it from running anyway. Actually when a run is cancelled, GitHub cancels all pending jobs. So factory would be cancelled anyway. The `duplicate` output is belt-and-suspenders.

   Wait, actually there's a real concern: `gh run cancel` on the current run from within itself — does it work? Yes, it's a known pattern; the API accepts it and the run gets cancelled. Though there can be a race where the cancel API returns success but the run completes before cancellation takes effect. The `exit 0` ensures the job doesn't fail. But the run's conclusion would be "cancelled" — fine.

   Actually a subtle bug: if `gh run cancel` fails (e.g., permissions), the run continues as successful and factory is skipped via the output. OK, that's handled.

2. **ANCHOR mismatch between run-name token and displayTitle matching**: The dedupe matches the anchor token in `displayTitle`. The run-name is:
   ```
   ▶ {leg} (SM) · pr-{pr} or gh-{issue} · {title}
   ```
   or for issues events:
   ```
   '⚒️ dev' · gh-{issue.number}{: title}
   ```
   
   Wait — for `issues` events, the run name is `'⚒️ dev · gh-305: <issue title>'`. The displayTitle for a workflow run is the run name. So matching `test("(^|[^0-9])gh-305([^0-9]|$)")` — the title could contain "gh-305" elsewhere. The regex `(^|[^0-9])gh-305([^0-9]|$)` requires the token be delimited by non-digits. Reasonable.

   BUT: an important issue — the token `gh-<issue>` may legitimately appear in the issue TITLE itself! E.g., issue title "Fix gh-305 regression" — wait, but that would only match if the title contains the exact same anchor token as the current run's anchor. If issue #305's title mentions "gh-305"... unlikely coincidence but possible. More importantly: an issue whose title references the same issue number (e.g. rework labels re-fire with run name "🔧 rework · gh-305: Fix bug in gh-305"). Hmm, edge case. Not blocking.

3. **Match ignores the LEG dimension**: Two runs on the same issue with different legs (dev vs review) — e.g., dispatch dev leg for gh-305 while a review leg for gh-305 is in progress. Both have tokens `gh-305`. The dedupe would self-cancel the second leg even though it's a DIFFERENT leg (review vs dev). Is that a problem? The concurrency group already serializes them (cancel-in-progress: false), so they queue. With this gate, the second one (different leg!) self-cancels entirely rather than queueing. Hmm — is that intended? The PR title says "identical live leg self-cancels". But the gate doesn't compare legs — it only compares the anchor. A legitimate queued review leg would be cancelled because a dev leg is running. Wait — but would that be a real scenario? Issues events: assigned → dev leg, labeled agent:review → review leg. If a dev leg is in progress on the same issue and someone adds the review label, the new run self-cancels. Previously it would queue behind. Is this a behavior regression? # Control the concurrency of workflows and jobs

Manage which workflows and jobs can run simultaneously.

Copy markdown

## In this article

## Using concurrency in different scenarios

You can use `jobs.<job_id>.concurrency` to ensure that only a single job or workflow using the same concurrency group will run at a time. A concurrency group can be any string or expression. Allowed expression contexts: [`github`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#github-context), [`inputs`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#inputs-context), [`vars`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#vars-context), [`needs`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#needs-context), [`strategy`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#strategy-context), and [`matrix`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#matrix-context). For more information about expressions, see [Evaluate expressions in workflows and actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions).

You can also specify `concurrency` at the workflow level. For more information, see [`concurrency`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#concurrency).

This means that there can be at most one running job or workflow in a concurrency group at any time. When a concurrent job or workflow is queued, if another job or workflow using the same concurrency group in the repository is in progress, the queued job or workflow will be `pending`. By default, any existing `pending` job or workflow in the same concurrency group will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place.

To also cancel any currently running job or workflow in the same concurrency group, specify `cancel-in-progress: true`. To conditionally cancel currently running jobs or workflows in the same concurrency group, you can specify `cancel-in-progress` as an expression with any of the allowed expression contexts.

To allow more than one `pending` job or workflow run to wait in the same concurrency group, use the optional `queue` property. The `queue` property accepts the following values:

- `single` (default): At most one job or workflow run can be `pending` in the concurrency group. When a new job or workflow run is queued, any existing `pending` job or workflow run in the same group is canceled and replaced.
- `max`: Up to 100 jobs or workflow runs can be `pending` in the concurrency group. When the queue is full, any additional jobs or workflow runs are canceled.

The combination of `queue: max` and `cancel-in-progress: true` is not allowed and will result in a workflow validation error.

Note

- The concurrency group name is case insensitive. For example, `prod` and `Prod` will be treated as the same concurrency group.
- Jobs or workflow runs in the same concurrency group are processed in first-in-first-out (FIFO) order according to the time each one started waiting on the concurrency group, not the time each workflow was dispatched. Since the actual start time of a job or run may vary, ordering is not guaranteed.

The default behavior of GitHub Actions is to allow multiple jobs or workflow runs to run concurrently. The `concurrency` keyword allows you to control the concurrency of workflow runs.

For example, you can use the `concurrency` keyword immediately after where trigger conditions are defined to limit the concurrency of entire workflow runs for a specific branch:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

concurrency:

  cancel-in-progress: true
```

```yaml

  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: example-group
      cancel-in-progress: true
```

### Example: Concurrency groups

Concurrency groups provide a way to manage and limit the execution of workflow runs or jobs that share the same concurrency key.

The `concurrency` key is used to group workflows or jobs together into a concurrency group. When you define a `concurrency` key, GitHub Actions ensures that only one workflow or job with that key runs at any given time. If a new workflow run or job starts with the same `concurrency` key, GitHub Actions will cancel any workflow or job already running with that key. The `concurrency` key can be a hard-coded string, or it can be a dynamic expression that includes context variables.

It is possible to define concurrency conditions in your workflow so that the workflow or job is part of a concurrency group.

This means that when a workflow run or job starts, GitHub will cancel any workflow runs or jobs that are already in progress in the same concurrency group. This is useful in scenarios where you want to prevent parallel runs for a certain set of a workflows or jobs, such as the ones used for deployments to a staging environment, in order to prevent actions that could cause conflicts or consume more resources than necessary.

In this example, `job-1` is part of a concurrency group named `staging_environment`. This means that if a new run of `job-1` is triggered, any runs of the same job in the `staging_environment` concurrency group that are already in progress will be cancelled.

By default, only one job or workflow run can be `pending` in a concurrency group at a time. To allow multiple runs to queue instead of being canceled, set `queue: max`. With `queue: max`, up to 100 jobs or workflow runs can wait in the concurrency group; once the queue is full, any additional runs are canceled.

For example, the following workflow queues deployments to the `production` environment, processing them one at a time in order based on when each run started waiting on the concurrency group:


To use concurrency to cancel any in-progress job or run in GitHub Actions, you can use the `concurrency` key with the `cancel-in-progress` option set to `true`:


The gate lists only `in_progress`/`queued`/`pending` runs, but a same-anchor twin **cannot be live when this job evaluates**: per [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/using-concurrency), a run queued behind a `cancel-in-progress: false` group stays `pending` until the in-progress run **completes**, and only then do its jobs start. So the younger twin's `dedupe` job always executes *after* the older run finished — `LIVE` is 0 — and the duplicate leg runs anyway.

The cited incident proves the shape: twin `36767943650` was created +113s after holder `36767724353`, sat `pending` for 23 minutes, and never dequeued before being cancelled at 20:09:44 (holder completed 20:15:37). With this gate, its dedupe would have run at ~20:16, found the holder `completed` (not listed), and dispatched a second full dev leg. The gate's effective window is only the first ~minute of the older run's life (while its own `dedupe` step runs); a twin arriving later — the "minutes apart" case in the PR description — is invisible to it.

**Suggested fix (the two halves pair; neither alone suffices):**
1. Also match **recently completed** runs, so the dequed twin sees the just-finished holder: list `--status completed --created=>$(date -u -d '10 min ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)` and self-cancel on a match. This catches the serialized twin with true first-wins (the holder already ran).
2. See the comment on `select(.databaseId != $self)` — without the `<` fix there, the older run self-cancels on sight of a pending younger twin.

Alternative structural fix: dedupe at the event level — one manual launch fires both `assigned` and `labeled`, so gate one of them at trigger/`jobs.<job>.if` level (e.g. only `agent:review`/`agent:rework` labels launch legs) instead of trying to detect twins at run time, where the group guarantees they can't be seen live.

Secondary note: the match is leg-blind (anchor only) — with the completed-window fix, a legitimate review/rework leg dequeued just after a dev leg on the same issue would self-cancel too. If per-leg semantics are wanted, include the run-name leg marker (`⚒️`/`🔍`/`🔧`/`▶ <leg> (SM)`) in the token.

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: `!= $self` inverts first-wins — the *older* run self-cancels on sight of a pending younger twin**

The repo's run history shows the dominant twin pattern is near-simultaneous dispatch (~1s apart: `issues` `assigned`+`labeled` fire back-to-back). In that case the younger run exists and is `pending` while the older run's `dedupe` step executes — so the older gate sees it, `LIVE > 0`, and the **older** run cancels itself. The younger twin then deques into a freed group, finds nothing live, and runs: last-wins, the opposite of the "first-wins" this PR titles. (It still yields one leg for ~1s twins, but by cancelling the wrong survivor — and a pending twin from a *different* leg, e.g. `🔍 review` dispatched seconds after `⚒️ dev`, starves the dev leg entirely.)

Filter to strictly older holders so the survivor is deterministic:

```jq
| select(.databaseId < $self)
```

Note: paired with the live-only check this alone reintroduces the double-fire (the dequed younger twin finds nothing live) — it must ship together with the recently-completed window from the comment on the `LIVE=` listing line.

# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# ALL logic lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory/
# teammate.yml (guard, legs, verdict, sessions, memory). This file carries
# only what cannot live in a reusable workflow: the repository event
# triggers, the per-issue concurrency group, and the call itself.
#
#   issue assigned/labeled → factory guard → dev/review/rework leg
#   workflow_dispatch (SM / manual) → leg pinned by input
#
# Secrets (explicit mapping): SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN (required by the factory),
# Vars: FA_VERSION_MACHINE || FA_VERSION || latest, DMTOOLS_VERSION,
# ZAI_CODE_KEY, KIMI_REVIEW_KEY (optional provider keys).
# MAX_AUTO_REWORK_ROUNDS.

name: 'AI Teammate'

run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      format('▶ {0} (SM) · {1}', github.event.inputs.leg,
        (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
        || format('gh-{0}', github.event.inputs.issue)) ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:rework' && '🔧 rework' ||
      github.event.label.name == 'agent:review' && '🔍 review' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:rework') && '🔧 rework' ||
      contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'agent:review') && '🔍 review' ||
      '⚒️ dev' }}
  · ${{ (github.event.inputs.pr || '') != '' && format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr)
      || format('gh-{0}', github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue) }}${{
      github.event.issue.title && format(': {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}

on:
  issues:
    types: [assigned, labeled]  # dev leg; review/rework ride labels too
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue:
        description: 'Issue number to run the agent on (empty for PR-anchored runs, #687)'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''
      leg:
        description: 'Which leg to run'
        required: true
        type: choice
        options: [dev, review, rework]
      reason:
        description: 'Why this dispatch (audit trail, shown in logs)'
        required: false
        type: string
      pr:
        description: 'PR number for PR-anchored review runs (#687) — the SM dispatches review with pr instead of issue'
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ''

concurrency:
  # PR-anchored dispatches (#544/#687) carry no issue — fall back to the pr
  # input so each PR keeps its OWN group ('ai-teammate-issue-pr-266');
  # without it every PR-anchored run shares the empty group and serializes
  # across unrelated PRs.
  group: ai-teammate-issue-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  dedupe:
    # First-wins: the `issues` trigger fires on assigned AND labeled, so one
    # manual launch can dispatch two dev legs minutes apart (live gh-305 twin,
    # 2026-09-30: 36767724353 in_progress + 36767943650 pending behind the
    # concurrency group, both event=issues). The concurrency group only
    # SERIALIZES twins — this gate makes the younger run self-cancel when an
    # older live run of this workflow already anchors the same issue/pr.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status in_progress --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status queued    --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                    gh run list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --workflow ai-teammate.yml --status pending   --json databaseId,displayTitle --jq '.[]'
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

  factory:
    needs: dedupe
    if: needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true'
    # Pinned to the immutable SHA the `agents` submodule pins — a branch
    # ref executes the branch head at run start, and the head has since
    # renamed the reusable workflows away from factory/<name>.yml. This
    # commit has the called paths and the self-pin that checks out
    # factory-agents/ at the same SHA. Flip in lockstep with the
    # submodule when dmtools-agents#424 merges (bump the submodule,
    # then repoint this ref at the new SHA).
    # Guarded by test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-teammate.yml@0176b270314aba9dcbd70732db558a156b03df04
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 0176b270314aba9dcbd70732db558a156b03df04
      # Bitrise Build Hub pool (epam-org visible; probe #229).
      runner: bitrise-runner-dmtools-ci
      issue: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue }}
      leg: ${{ github.event.inputs.leg || '' }}
      reason: ${{ github.event.inputs.reason || 'stub' }}
      pr: ${{ github.event.inputs.pr || '' }}
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
      ZAI_CODE_KEY: ${{ secrets.ZAI_CODE_KEY }}
      KIMI_REVIEW_KEY: ${{ secrets.KIMI_REVIEW_KEY }}
# DMTOOLS_PACK_REGISTRY (pack registry base) is read by the factory from
# this repo's VARIABLE of the same name — see dmtools-agents#574.

Now let me analyze this change carefully. The PR adds a `dedupe` job to the `ai-teammate.yml` workflow. Let me look at the details:

```yaml
jobs:
  dedupe:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      duplicate: ${{ steps.gate.outputs.duplicate }}
    steps:
      - name: Self-cancel if an identical live leg already holds the anchor
        id: gate
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          ANCHOR: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.inputs.issue || format('pr-{0}', github.event.inputs.pr) }}
        run: |
          case "$ANCHOR" in
            pr-*) T="$ANCHOR" ;;
            *)    T="gh-$ANCHOR" ;;
          esac
          LIVE=$( { gh run list ... --status in_progress ...
                    gh run list ... --status queued ...
                    gh run list ... --status pending ...
                  } | jq -s --argjson self '${{ github.run_id }}' --arg t "$T" '
                    [ .[]
                      | select(.databaseId != $self)
                      | select(.displayTitle | test("(^|[^0-9])" + $t + "([^0-9]|$)")) ]
                    | length')
          if [ "${LIVE:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::notice::identical live leg holds $T — cancelling this duplicate ($LIVE holder(s) found)"
            echo "duplicate=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            gh run cancel "${{ github.run_id }}" -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" || true
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "duplicate=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
```

Issues to consider:

1. **Self-cancel race / fallthrough behavior**: When a duplicate is detected, the step sets `duplicate=true`, then calls `gh run cancel` on itself, then `exit 0`. The job continues (exits 0 → success). The `factory` job is skipped due to the `if`. But the run shows as "success" while also being cancelled — the `gh run cancel` is async; the run gets status cancelled eventually. This is a bit odd but works. Actually wait — there's a subtlety: `gh run cancel` cancels the entire run, which would cancel this very `dedupe` job mid-flight. But before that, the step writes `duplicate=true` and exits 0. When the run is cancelled, the `factory` job... hmm, the factory job's `if: needs.dedupe.outputs.duplicate != 'true'` would prevent it from running anyway. Actually when a run is cancelled, GitHub cancels all pending jobs. So factory would be cancelled anyway. The `duplicate` output is belt-and-suspenders.

   Wait, actually there's a real concern: `gh run cancel` on the current run from within itself — does it work? Yes, it's a known pattern; the API accepts it and the run gets cancelled. Though there can be a race where the cancel API returns success but the run completes before cancellation takes effect. The `exit 0` ensures the job doesn't fail. But the run's conclusion would be "cancelled" — fine.

   Actually a subtle bug: if `gh run cancel` fails (e.g., permissions), the run continues as successful and factory is skipped via the output. OK, that's handled.

2. **ANCHOR mismatch between run-name token and displayTitle matching**: The dedupe matches the anchor token in `displayTitle`. The run-name is:
   ```
   ▶ {leg} (SM) · pr-{pr} or gh-{issue} · {title}
   ```
   or for issues events:
   ```
   '⚒️ dev' · gh-{issue.number}{: title}
   ```
   
   Wait — for `issues` events, the run name is `'⚒️ dev · gh-305: <issue title>'`. The displayTitle for a workflow run is the run name. So matching `test("(^|[^0-9])gh-305([^0-9]|$)")` — the title could contain "gh-305" elsewhere. The regex `(^|[^0-9])gh-305([^0-9]|$)` requires the token be delimited by non-digits. Reasonable.

   BUT: an important issue — the token `gh-<issue>` may legitimately appear in the issue TITLE itself! E.g., issue title "Fix gh-305 regression" — wait, but that would only match if the title contains the exact same anchor token as the current run's anchor. If issue #305's title mentions "gh-305"... unlikely coincidence but possible. More importantly: an issue whose title references the same issue number (e.g. rework labels re-fire with run name "🔧 rework · gh-305: Fix bug in gh-305"). Hmm, edge case. Not blocking.

3. **Match ignores the LEG dimension**: Two runs on the same issue with different legs (dev vs review) — e.g., dispatch dev leg for gh-305 while a review leg for gh-305 is in progress. # Control the concurrency of workflows and jobs

Manage which workflows and jobs can run simultaneously.

Copy markdown

## In this article

## Using concurrency in different scenarios

You can use `jobs.<job_id>.concurrency` to ensure that only a single job or workflow using the same concurrency group will run at a time. A concurrency group can be any string or expression. Allowed expression contexts: [`github`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#github-context), [`inputs`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#inputs-context), [`vars`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#vars-context), [`needs`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#needs-context), [`strategy`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#strategy-context), and [`matrix`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/contexts#matrix-context). For more information about expressions, see [Evaluate expressions in workflows and actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/expressions).

You can also specify `concurrency` at the workflow level. For more information, see [`concurrency`](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#concurrency).

This means that there can be at most one running job or workflow in a concurrency group at any time. When a concurrent job or workflow is queued, if another job or workflow using the same concurrency group in the repository is in progress, the queued job or workflow will be `pending`. By default, any existing `pending` job or workflow in the same concurrency group will be canceled and the new queued job or workflow will take its place.

To also cancel any currently running job or workflow in the same concurrency group, specify `cancel-in-progress: true`. To conditionally cancel currently running jobs or workflows in the same concurrency group, you can specify `cancel-in-progress` as an expression with any of the allowed expression contexts.

To allow more than one `pending` job or workflow run to wait in the same concurrency group, use the optional `queue` property. The `queue` property accepts the following values:

- `single` (default): At most one job or workflow run can be `pending` in the concurrency group. When a new job or workflow run is queued, any existing `pending` job or workflow run in the same group is canceled and replaced.
- `max`: Up to 100 jobs or workflow runs can be `pending` in the concurrency group. When the queue is full, any additional jobs or workflow runs are canceled.

The combination of `queue: max` and `cancel-in-progress: true` is not allowed and will result in a workflow validation error.

Note

- The concurrency group name is case insensitive. For example, `prod` and `Prod` will be treated as the same concurrency group.
- Jobs or workflow runs in the same concurrency group are processed in first-in-first-out (FIFO) order according to the time each one started waiting on the concurrency group, not the time each workflow was dispatched. Since the actual start time of a job or run may vary, ordering is not guaranteed.

### Example: Using concurrency and the default behavior

The default behavior of GitHub Actions is to allow multiple jobs or workflow runs to run concurrently. The `concurrency` keyword allows you to control the concurrency of workflow runs.

For example, you can use the `concurrency` keyword immediately after where trigger conditions are defined to limit the concurrency of entire workflow runs for a specific branch:

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

```yaml
on:
  push:
    branches:

jobs:

    concurrency:
      group: example-group
      cancel-in-progress: true
```

### Example: Concurrency groups

Concurrency groups provide a way to manage and limit the execution of workflow runs or jobs that share the same concurrency key.

The `concurrency` key is used to group workflows or jobs together into a concurrency group. When you define a `concurrency` key, GitHub Actions ensures that only one workflow or job with that key runs at any given time. If a new workflow run or job starts with the same `concurrency` key, GitHub Actions will cancel any workflow or job already running with that key. The `concurrency` key can be a hard-coded string, or it can be a dynamic expression that includes context variables.

It is possible to define concurrency conditions in your workflow so that the workflow or job is part of a concurrency group.

This means that when a workflow run or job starts, GitHub will cancel any workflow runs or jobs that are already in progress in the same concurrency group. This is useful in scenarios where you want to prevent parallel runs for a certain set of a workflows or jobs, such as the ones used for deployments to a staging environment, in order to prevent actions that could cause conflicts or consume more resources than necessary.

In this example, `job-1` is part of a concurrency group named `staging_environment`. This means that if a new run of `job-1` is triggered, any runs of the same job in the `staging_environment` concurrency group that are already in progress will be cancelled.

By default, only one job or workflow run can be `pending` in a concurrency group at a time. To allow multiple runs to queue instead of being canceled, set `queue: max`. With `queue: max`, up to 100 jobs or workflow runs can wait in the concurrency group; once the queue is full, any additional runs are canceled.

For example, the following workflow queues deployments to the `production` environment, processing them one at a time in order based on when each run started waiting on the concurrency group:

```yaml

    branches:

concurrency:
  group: production-deploy

```

Note that `queue: max` cannot be combined with `cancel-in-progress: true`, because the two options describe conflicting behaviors for handling in-progress runs.

To use concurrency to cancel any in-progress job or run in GitHub Actions, you can use the `concurrency` key with the `cancel-in-progress` option set to `true`:

```yaml

```

{"path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","content":"🚨 **BLOCKING: The live-run check cannot see the twins it targets — group-serialized duplicates still run a second leg**

The gate lists only `in_progress`/`queued`/`pending` runs, but a same-anchor twin **cannot be live when this job evaluates**: per [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/writing-workflows/choosing-what-your-workflow-does/using-concurrency), a run queued behind a `cancel-in-progress: false` group stays `pending` until the in-progress run **completes**, and only then do its jobs start. So the younger twin's `dedupe` job always executes *after* the older run finished — `LIVE` is 0 — and the duplicate leg runs anyway.

The cited incident proves the shape: twin `36767943650` was created +113s after holder `36767724353`, sat `pending` for 23 minutes, and never dequeued before being cancelled at 20:09:44 (holder completed 20:15:37). With this gate, its dedupe would have run at ~20:16, found the holder `completed` (not listed), and dispatched a second full dev leg. The gate's effective window is only the first ~minute of the older run's life (while its own `dedupe` step runs); a twin arriving later — the "minutes apart" case in the PR description — is invisible to it.

**Suggested fix (the two halves pair; neither alone suffices):**
1. Also match **recently completed** runs, so the dequed twin sees the just-finished holder: list `--status completed --created=>$(date -u -d '10 min ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)` and self-cancel on a match. This catches the serialized twin with true first-wins (the holder already ran).
2. See the comment on `select(.databaseId != $self)` — without the `<` fix there, the older run self-cancels on sight of a pending younger twin.

Alternative structural fix: dedupe at the event level — one manual launch fires both `assigned` and `labeled`, so gate one of them at trigger/`jobs.<job>.if` level (e.g. only `agent:review`/`agent:rework` labels launch legs) instead of trying to detect twins at run time, where the group guarantees they can't be seen live.

Secondary note: the match is leg-blind (anchor only) — with the completed-window fix, a legitimate review/rework leg dequeued just after a dev leg on the same issue would self-cancel too. If per-leg semantics are wanted, include the run-name leg marker (`⚒️`/`🔍`/`🔧`/`▶ <leg> (SM)`) in the token.
"}

⚠️ **IMPORTANT: Token regex matches the free-text issue-title suffix — false self-cancels from titles that merely mention the anchor**

`displayTitle` is the run name, which appends the raw issue title after the token (`· gh-305: <title>`). `test("(^|[^0-9])gh-305([^0-9]|$)")` therefore matches any live run whose *title text* contains `gh-305` — plausible in this repo, whose issue titles routinely embed cross-references (the live gh-305 title itself carries `(Java #592 / PR epam/dm.ai#619)`). Example verified against the real title format: a live run for issue 3050 titled `⚒️ dev\n· gh-3050: follow-up to gh-305` matches token `gh-305` via the title mention, so a **legitimate** gh-305 dispatch would self-cancel while no gh-305 leg is running — a silently dropped launch.

In the run-name template the anchor token is always preceded by `· ` and followed by `:` (then the title) or end-of-string. Anchor on that structure — verified against all observed variants (`⚒️ dev\n· gh-305: …`, `▶ rework (SM) · gh-305 · gh-305`, `▶ review (SM) · pr-308 · pr-308`):

```jq
| select(.displayTitle | test("· " + $t + "(:|$)"))
```

# PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only.

# AI Teammate — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
